package_info.package_manager: custom/Electron (distributed as MSI, DMG, NuGet, EXE)
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp package was compromised via a supply chain attack, resulting in the insertion of malicious code into standard DLL dependencies (ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll). The attack leveraged post-signing modification of a Microsoft-signed DLL to append encrypted shellcode, and altered the ffmpeg library to extract and execute this payload, enabling further malicious activity such as C2 communication and potential data exfiltration.

execution_context.trigger: At process startup, when ffmpeg.dll is loaded by 3CXDesktopApp

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Custom loader code in ffmpeg.dll that locates d3dcompiler_47.dll, searches for the magic signature 0xFEEDFACEFEEDFACE, extracts appended RC4-encrypted shellcode, and decrypts it using the key '3jB(2bsG#@c7'.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At process startup, the code in ffmpeg.dll locates d3dcompiler_47.dll, scans for the magic byte signature 0xFEEDFACEFEEDFACE, extracts the appended RC4-encrypted shellcode, decrypts it using the hardcoded RC4 key '3jB(2bsG#@c7', and loads the decrypted shellcode into memory for execution, enabling the next stage of the attack.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: ffmpeg.dll is a media processing library and should not contain code that searches for, decrypts, and executes shellcode from another DLL. The presence of cryptographic operations and inter-DLL memory manipulation is highly anomalous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate ffmpeg.dll should only handle media decoding/encoding and should not interact with other DLLs to extract or execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or anti-tampering solutions may use encrypted payloads, but not in this context or with these libraries, and never to execute arbitrary shellcode from another DLL.
key_indicators: Custom code in ffmpeg.dll for searching magic signature in d3dcompiler_47.dll
Hardcoded RC4 decryption key and cryptographic routines
Extraction and in-memory execution of decrypted shellcode
Reference to d3dcompiler_47.dll within a media library

execution_context.trigger: When loaded by ffmpeg.dll during process startup

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: RC4-encrypted shellcode appended after the authenticode signature, marked by the magic bytes 0xFEEDFACEFEEDFACE. The shellcode, once decrypted, contains an embedded DLL that downloads C2 URLs from GitHub icon files, decrypts them (AES, Base64), and initiates C2 communication.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When loaded by ffmpeg.dll during process startup, the RC4-encrypted shellcode appended to d3dcompiler_47.dll is identified by the magic signature, extracted, decrypted, and executed in memory. The shellcode contains an embedded DLL that initiates the next stage of the attack by downloading and decrypting C2 URLs.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Appending encrypted shellcode to a signed Microsoft DLL is a known malware technique to evade detection and abuse trust in signed binaries. The use of a magic signature and cryptographic obfuscation further indicates malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: d3dcompiler_47.dll should not contain any appended data, especially not executable or encrypted payloads, after its authenticode signature.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Appending non-executable metadata for tracking or versioning is sometimes done, but never encrypted shellcode or executable payloads.
key_indicators: Appended data after authenticode signature in d3dcompiler_47.dll
Embedded downloader logic for C2 URLs

execution_context.trigger: During shellcode execution in memory after decryption by ffmpeg.dll

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Downloader logic in shellcode: fetches icon files from GitHub, extracts AES-encrypted, Base64-encoded C2 URLs from file ends, decrypts them, and connects to C2 infrastructure.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During in-memory shellcode execution, the code downloads icon files from GitHub repositories, extracts AES-encrypted and Base64-encoded C2 URLs hidden at the end of these files, decrypts the URLs, and establishes outbound network connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling command and control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate software does not hide C2 URLs in icon files on GitHub or use shellcode to establish covert C2 channels. The use of steganography and cryptography to conceal C2 infrastructure is a hallmark of advanced malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal update or telemetry mechanisms are transparent, use documented endpoints, and do not employ encrypted, hidden channels or covert data extraction from image files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate software uses this combination of steganography, cryptography, and covert network communication for update or telemetry purposes.
key_indicators: Network access to GitHub for non-standard resources (icon/image files)
Extraction of hidden data from image/icon files using AES and Base64 decoding
Outbound connections to attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Malicious ffmpeg.dll is included in the 3CXDesktopApp build, replacing the legitimate version.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious ffmpeg.dll is loaded at application startup.

attack_chain.action: ffmpeg.dll, upon loading, locates d3dcompiler_47.dll and extracts RC4-encrypted shellcode from its signature appendix.
attack_chain.leads_to: Shellcode is decrypted and executed in memory.

attack_chain.action: Decrypted shellcode (embedded DLL) downloads icon files from GitHub, extracts and decrypts C2 URLs, and connects to attacker infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishes C2 channel for further attacker actions (e.g., data exfiltration, remote access).

behavioral_signatures: DLLs (ffmpeg.dll) performing inter-DLL memory operations and in-memory shellcode execution
Extraction and decryption of appended data from signed DLLs (d3dcompiler_47.dll) using hardcoded cryptographic keys
Network requests to GitHub for icon/image files followed by AES/Base64 decryption of hidden C2 URLs
Outbound connections to non-standard, attacker-controlled infrastructure not associated with 3CX
file_indicators: ffmpeg.dll with increased file size and stripped PDB/debug data compared to official releases
d3dcompiler_47.dll with appended data after authenticode signature, containing magic signature 0xFEEDFACEFEEDFACE
Presence of magic signature 0xFEEDFACEFEEDFACE in DLL appendices
Unusual compilation timestamps or digital signature anomalies in ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to GitHub repositories for icon/image files (e.g., .ico, .png) not used by the application UI
Extraction and decryption of hidden data from downloaded files using AES and Base64
Outbound connections to C2 domains/IPs not associated with 3CX or its infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for DLLs (especially ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll) with appended data after authenticode signatures, increased file size, or stripped PDB/debug data. Flag binaries that perform inter-DLL memory operations or extract and decrypt shellcode at runtime using hardcoded cryptographic keys. Detect network activity involving downloads of non-standard resources (e.g., icon files) from GitHub, followed by AES/Base64 decryption and connections to unknown external infrastructure. Use differential analysis to compare new releases with previous versions for unexplained changes in standard libraries, and correlate with anomalous network activity to non-3CX domains.
